title: Neighbourhood bakery in Ohio
subtitle: Bread from wholesale flour, as of 15 May 2025
text: We are a neighbourhood bakery in Columbus, Ohio, and sell about 1,200 loaves a week. A loaf sells for $7 and costs about $2.40 to make; flour is about a third of that. The mill delivers weekly and we keep about 2 weeks of flour. The supermarket bakery sells a similar loaf for $5.50. I could put $6,000 into stock.

series.label: US hard red winter wheat price

what_happened.text: The World Bank's monthly price for US hard red winter wheat stayed between $231 and $246 a tonne from May to November 2025, against $237 in May.

caveats: Flour is about a third of a loaf's cost in the owner's own words. Flour prices follow wheat with milling and freight on top, so they move less than wheat in percent.
The series is US hard red winter wheat (Pink Sheet, monthly, $/mt), the usual bread wheat. It is a 'nothing happened' case: the news in spring 2025 was about tariffs, but wheat stayed flat.
Each monthly value is treated as the month's mid-point, with straight lines between them.
